China Revolutionizes Car Theft, With a BYD EV Stolen Right in Front of the Customer During Delivery
6 photos
Photo: Autohome
We've already known that whatever the Western companies do, Chinese companies do faster and cheaper. Unfortunately, this is also true for car theft, with a BYD Song EV stolen right in front of its future owner during the delivery process. At the time, the car was supposed to get its windows tinted, but the car just vanished from the lot.
Due to modern vehicles featuring advanced car-theft protection, car thieves are among the most resourceful in the business. They have to master high-tech methods to defeat anti-theft measures that carmakers integrate into their vehicles. However, most of the time, social engineering still works pretty well. A recent case in China shows that local thieves might be ahead of their peers from Western countries.
The buyer of a BYD Song EV saw their car stolen right in front of them, while awaiting delivery at the dealership. Worse, the future owner was an older man who was gifted the car to celebrate his 60th birthday. Instead of the festive moment he thought it would be, the moment turned into an adventure to secure the car after it was stolen during the delivery process.
Specifically, the customer requested the dealership to tint the windows before delivery. His family had paid 155,000 yuan ($21,500) in full for the car. They had just completed the paperwork, including invoicing and the temporary registration and license plate. Around 6 PM, while they were waiting in the customer lounge for the car to be washed and fitted with window film, a salesperson informed them that the vehicle had disappeared.
What looked like a perfectly normal celebratory moment turned into a full-time adventure as the family and dealership staff tried to locate and seize the stolen vehicle. After a chase that lasted more than an hour and covered over 20 km, they managed to intercept the car. The police took the driver into custody shortly afterward, putting an end to the drama.
While thieves stealing cars from dealerships are nothing new , this one used an ingenious method to do it in the middle of the day, without raising concerns. The suspect was dressed as a BYD employee at the time of his arrest. This made everyone suspicious that it was an inside job. However, upon closer inspection, the uniform did not quite match those worn by actual staff at the dealership.
The investigation revealed that the thief had never been an employee of a BYD dealership, and he bought the BYD-branded uniform online. The suspect had a prior record of car theft , and he was apparently "mentally unstable." However, questions still remain about security lapses at the BYD dealership that allowed the thief to steal the car during the delivery process.
In the aftermath of the event , the family declined to take delivery of the previously stolen vehicle. They have also requested punitive "triple damages" under Chinese customer protection laws. However, the dealership rejected the demand, arguing that they were also victims of the theft. Instead, they agreed to refund the full payment of the car and the insurance policy. The dealership also reimbursed the family for the round-trip travel and lodging expenses.
